questions.q: The product of heating pinacol with concentrated H₂SO₄ is:
questions.explain: Loss of water gives a tertiary carbocation, a methyl group shifts 1,2, and the oxonium ion loses H⁺ to give pinacolone, (CH₃)₃C–CO–CH₃.

questions.q: In the pinacol rearrangement, the correct order of migratory aptitude is roughly:
questions.explain: The group that best shares the positive charge during the shift moves; aryl migrates most readily, then hydride, then alkyl, with methyl among the poorest.

questions.q: What is the driving force of the pinacol–pinacolone rearrangement?
options: Formation of an alkene by loss of a second water molecule
Relief of ring strain in the diol
Conversion of a carbocation into a resonance-stabilised oxonium ion that becomes a C=O bond
questions.explain: After the 1,2-shift the charge sits on the carbon bearing OH, stabilised as an oxonium ion; losing H⁺ gives a strong C=O bond.

questions.q: Cyclohexylidenecyclohexane is treated with OsO₄ followed by aqueous work-up, and the diol is heated with H⁺. The final product is:
questions.explain: OsO₄ gives the syn diol; after one OH leaves, a ring C–C bond of the other ring migrates, expanding it to a seven-membered cycloheptanone spiro-fused to cyclohexane. Spiro[4.5]decan-6-one comes from the bi(cyclopentyl) diol.
